text: Let's begin Lesson 7.
In this lesson, we will talk about journaling.

In the previous modules, we focused on controlling your time, setting goals, breaking them down, putting tasks into your calendar—and that matters, and that is the most important stuff for the thing which will move the needle.
But even with a perfect plan, you can still wake up and have a bad day.
You can still wake
up and feel emotionally sad, emotionally angry, emotionally disappointed.
And you can kind of feel sometimes that there is a bit of chaos in your life, even though you definitely know exactly what to do.

You have your big goal, you have broken it down, and you're using your calendar to execute it, but you still sometimes wake up or go to bed a little bit confused, and a little bit having not the best day possible.

The thing to note is that most bad days don't come from one big mistake, from one big thing which, like a giant light flashing at you, tells you, 'This is the big mistake, this is the big thing that you need to fix,' but they mostly are small things, like just a little bit of mental clutter, lack of clarity, feeling slightly out of control, just a little bit of something which happened in your mind
—just a negative thought, or just something where you were doing everything all right but something happened, but you don't really see it that much.
It is not that big of a thing where you can immediately know, 'This was the thing,' you know?
You don't really...
It is...
It is not really that easy to know, just by thinking in seconds, what is wrong in your day and life.
Just by thinking in seconds, it is not really possible to

go deep into your mind and know the real cause of why you are having this bad of a day or this feeling—because it's not, I guess, a bad day, but sometimes it may be some kind of feelings where you don't really feel all right.
And as an example, bad days start sometimes from the night before, you know?
When you're just in bed overthinking, imagining fake scenarios, and then after those, even when you go to sleep, you get a poor
night's sleep.

And then what happens is that you stay up late sometimes, and then you watch TV and eat bad snacks, and then the next morning goes bad as well, because you had a previous night which did not really go that well.

You wake up late, and then you start a negative day, even though you may know what you're doing and you can use the calendars and everything to still schedule your day, but you, in the back of your mind,
tell yourself that you could have had a better day.
You know that you made some wrong choices, and those wrong choices, again, they may start from just a little bit of a thing.

It can just start from just overthinking, and then imagining some fake scenarios, and then going into the negative route of thinking, and then staying up all night, and then having, for the rest of the day, something bad.
But in here again, it's just, in this example, someone

thinking this thing: 'I'm just lazy, I'm just not disciplined, I can't control my life, I am nobody, I shouldn't do this, I will always be doomed, I'm not able to achieve anything in my life.' And then the negative thoughts just keep on going, and then, you know, the parts of like what happens after that where you just go negative after negative after negative stuff, and then when you think negatively, negative stuff will definitely
happen.
But in this case, if this person were to go deeper, he would have just found out that the solution—or the problem—just came from just thinking too much, just overthinking before bed.

And then that overthinking brought a fake scenario—like, it's not even real, it's fake, it's something which you made up in your mind—and from that, it happened that you stayed up late watching TV and doing something which you didn't want to do, and then you ended up having a
bad morning, and then bad days follow after that.
And again, it all started from just one little thought, just one little bit of imagining a fake scenario, something negative which you may have imagined.
But again, this doesn't flash a light at you saying that this is the problem.
You overthink just for a little bit; there's no flashlight or big light which you can see to say, 'Okay, that is the problem.' For this, you have to go deeper to notice what the
problem is.
And the problem with most people is that when they have a bad day, when they feel bad, when they don't feel good, most people don't stop.
What they do is just they grab their phone, they scroll and distract themselves, and avoid thinking.
And we see this, in my opinion, as one of the biggest problems in today's society.
I think this is why the world is not really in the best way that it should be, and why so
many people are depressed and they don't like their lives.
They don't know what to do, they don't know where to go, and they just have terrible lives.
And the reason behind that is because they never stop; they never stop and think, they never stop and go deeper into their mind because they have so many problems.
And if they just think for just a second, just a minute, if they were to start and think, they would run away like somebody

was trying to kill them, because they can't handle the big pressure and all of the terrible things which are going on in their life—all of the things which they want to do but they are not doing, all of the things which they are leaving on the table, and all of the bad things which they are doing day-to-day, and all of their life just feeling completely out of control.
You can definitely notice, I would say, 80 to 90% of people nowadays, you never
see them thinking.
You never see them trying to solve their problems, trying to go deeper within themselves to solve their problems.
And I want you to notice that it's quite interesting: whenever they have just a single minute—it's like...
it's funny...
they have a single minute when they don't have their phone, maybe they were talking with somebody and then the conversation ended, just a single minute—they start to think.
And I agree with that, of course, but one of the biggest things, in my opinion, is that they can't handle their thoughts.
It's too much pressure, it's too many problems, and what to do?
Grab your phone, distract yourself, distract yourself from doing the problems, from solving the problems, from thinking about the problems, because it hurts.
It freaking hurts; it hurts even more than doing physical workouts.
It beats
doing something which usually is hard to do.

And I will say that trying to solve your problems in your mind, trying to go deeper in your mind, is harder than working out, is harder than studying, is harder than doing whatever you think is really hard.
And if you haven't done so, if you haven't really taken your time to stay alone sometimes and think, think about your life, if you haven't done that, please go ahead and do that.
It's one of the hardest things to do.
And as the famous quote, I guess,
goes, 'Most men's problems come because they can't stay in a room alone for 30 minutes.' And it's freaking true.

And even if you do 30 minutes, there are the moments when something bad happens, when you're feeling something very bad and you don't like that emotion at all, and it's such a big pull to just grab your phone and just distract yourself to not feel that feeling anymore, because it hurts.
That is the part where you
go there and think.
At that moment when there is a feeling you don't really know why you're feeling that way, and for you to find the solution, you know that you have to go deeper.

You know that you have to go to the uncomfortable truths of your life, but in that time, the amount of pull to just grab your phone and just distract yourself with whatever—even if not having a phone, something else—it's so, so big.
And it tells how much we are lacking thinking
deeper within our minds.
And so the problem is not that your life is out of control.
It's not that, again, you don't have the goal now.

It's not that you haven't broken it down, it's not that you don't know what to do today, it's not that you're not using a calendar, it's not that you're not managing your goals or whatever, as we have taught in the previous lecture.
But now, it's something deeper within you.
You don't really see what is happening deep inside you,
which is calling out to you, but throughout the years, you have just pushed it down and you have just forgotten it.
And what we need to do is go deeper, and when we go deeper, we understand why our days go bad and good.
You stop guessing, like, 'This is a big thing, it is because of this.' No, you actually know.
You go deeper, and you see that it's completely something which you did not see at all; it's something way deeper in there.
You stop blaming yourself,
and stop blaming even other people, because a lot of people blame other people because they're having bad days, bad lives, whatever.
But in reality, it's them.
It's something within them that they are not fixing, and once you go deeper, you know what to fix.

And for me, quite recently, when a lot of stuff was happening—I was building this course, I was starting a new app (I actually started two different apps), unsure where to begin, unsure what to do, I did not really know the timeline of completing the course—it was
quite a stressful time.
I didn't really know: What am I actually doing?
Should I really do this one?
Should I really start these apps?
Where do I even begin?
How much longer will this take me?
And for me, I was just not really answering those questions.
I was going day-by-day, feeling those feelings, and not answering those questions.
And even though I was doing the work, even though I was creating this course, even though I was creating the apps and doing the stuff which I set out to do, I was just feeling these
painful emotions.
I was just feeling these negative emotions which I was not liking.
And so what I did: I just grabbed a notebook.
That's it—just a notebook.
No rules, no system, no structure.
I just wrote everything in my head, everything which was going on with the course, with the apps—and not that the course was the problem, but all the deeper stuff, all of the other stuff in my life.
I just wrote everything down, and once everything was written down,
everything made much more sense.
Not because my problems disappeared, but now I can see the solutions, now I can see the problem.
I can see that there was something deeper.
It was not really the course that much, it was not really the apps and stuff like this; it was just clarifying that I'm on the right path, I'm doing the right stuff.
And you can definitely do it without a notebook, but a notebook is quite special because
you can see everything now.
It's like you're putting everything down, and now you can play with it, you know?
It's like toys: you put all of the problems, or you put all of the things which you think are the problem, but now you can actually visually see them.
It's not in here; you can't really manage it in here that easily.
But in here, in a notebook, you can see everything, and then again, you can play, and you can see what is the problem and what is the solution.
And this is not about the commitment—
don't get it wrong.

I'm not telling people to become a guy who journals just to say, 'Oh, I journal.' Or, I don't want to make you someone who just can say to others, 'Oh, I journal every day,' or can just say to yourself, 'Oh, I'm a person who journals, I have this great habit.' That's not my point.
And here, you don't need streaks, you don't need discipline, you don't need motivation to do this.
All we need in here is just a way to clear our mind, a way to understand ourselves
when things feel off, when there are things which are out of control, things which are deeper, as we said, because we need to dive deep within ourselves.
We need to put stuff down, and journaling is one of them.
You can definitely do it just by thinking and walking, and that is amazing, and you should definitely do that—and I do that as well.
But sometimes, again, you just need to put them on paper.
You need to see them visually, what the problem is, and try to answer that
problem, trying to go deeper—and that's what journaling is.

But to not go immediately into this list of what you need to do every day, or what in general you need to do with journaling, I will say that in the next lecture, where I will show you the simplest way to clear your thoughts with zero pressure and zero rules.
It's basically the example which I gave in this lesson.
